Maria Chen: :rotating_light: p95 up to 1.4s, p99 ~4.2s and a rise in 504/502 from the gateway since canary finished ~2m ago. Deploy ID 2026-03-15T10:12:30Z. Rolling back?
SRE-Bot: @Oncall Pager page sent to the SRE rotation (severity: high). Runbook: https://go/runbooks/timeout-regression
Oncall Pager: I'm on it, grabbing traces. Which route is spiking?
Maria Chen: Mostly TextGen endpoints and /v1/chat/stream. Customer-facing errors in EU region first.
Liam O'Connor: Looking at ingress logs — connection pools show a lot of lingering downstream sockets, gateway timing out at 120s and returning 504s. Could be a backend stall after the new kernel selection.
Priya Patel: Flagging to CS: we might have partial customer impact for interactive apps. Holding off external comms until we know rollback status.
Maria Chen: Deploy-bot, confirm canary host list and release tag?
deploy-bot: Canary completed: tag=rlz-0.37.2, hosts=canary-pset-7, finished at 1781122290. No automatic rollback triggered.
Liam O'Connor: Pulling runtime logs from canary hosts now. Attaching a short excerpt: ```
[2026-03-15T10:13:05Z] WARN request id=abc123 stage=kv-fetch duration=2150ms
[2026-03-15T10:13:07Z] ERROR request id=abc124 reason=async-kv-timeout status=504
[2026-03-15T10:13:11Z] WARN request id=abc125 kv-cache miss, queue-length=86
```
Maria Chen: That queue-length jump looks like a batching/backpressure loop. Any config changes in the release?
Liam O'Connor: Release notes show "improved kernel selection heuristics" and "aggressive continuous-batching" enabled behind feature flag. Suspecting batching param too aggressive for short-latency tail workloads.
Priya Patel: If we keep this live, more customers will see degraded interactive UX. Suggest immediate firebreak (rollback) and then investigation postmortem.
Maria Chen: Agreed. Rolling back canary to previous stable. deploy-bot, initiate rollback for tag=rlz-0.37.2 on canary-pset-7.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for canary-pset-7 -> target tag=rlz-0.37.1. ETA ~90s. Streaming logs: ```
[deploy-bot] 10:14:05 stopping canary-pset-7
[deploy-bot] 10:14:20 deploying rlz-0.37.1 to canary-pset-7
[deploy-bot] 10:15:30 healthchecks passing
```
Oncall Pager: Noticed error rate drop starting at 10:15:40. p99 down to ~0.9s. Connectivity errors trending down :thumbsup:.
Maria Chen: Can we confirm no queued requests or leak left? Liam, check kv cache eviction and socket states.
Liam O'Connor: Verified sockets returned to baseline, kv-cache hit rate recovered. Quick diff shows the batching window parameter `max_batch_ms` set from 5 -> 25 in this release for some models. That will amplify tail when requests are bursty.
Priya Patel: Noting impacted customers: two partners on EU read-only endpoints saw degraded SLAs, CS alerted. We'll prepare a short blurb if needed.
Maria Chen: I'm going to leave this thread open for postmortem notes. Action items: (1) revert the aggressive batching flag in next patch, (2) run a canary with traffic shaping, (3) prepare customer comms if we see follow-up incidents.
SRE-Bot: Incident opened: INC-2026-0315-17. Severity set to P1. Postmortem owner auto-assigned: Maria Chen. Link: https://go/incidents/INC-2026-0315-17
Liam O'Connor: I'll capture a minimal repro and the affected config diff and post to the incident ticket. Also adding logs and the sequence diagram for batching/backpressure.
Priya Patel: I'll draft a short internal note for CS/AE with timeline and mitigation. No public statement yet.
Maria Chen: Handoff to next oncall in 40m — leaving the incident in watch for 30m. If error rates reappear, escalate immediately. Thanks everyone for the rapid rollback. :heart:
Oncall Pager: Acknowledged handoff. Will monitor for 60m and update the ticket if anything resurfaces.
Maria Chen: Final note for the incident thread: root cause suspected regression in batching heuristics leading to request accumulation and gateway timeouts under bursty short-request patterns. Mitigation: rollback + revert feature flag. Postmortem to follow.
